defects.title: Doctor report publication turns a transient Windows sharing lock into a false Doctor command failure
defects.defect_class: diagnostic report publication / transient Windows sharing-lock resilience
defects.preconditions: DOCTOR_REPORT.json already exists and another Windows process temporarily holds an exclusive handle when Invoke-Doctor publishes the next report.
defects.bad_behavior: Invoke-Doctor can complete all health findings as OK and then exit 1 because its final DOCTOR_REPORT.json publication uses direct Set-Content. The report sink failure is surfaced as a Doctor command failure even though Manager/Hub health and durable state are unchanged.
defects.root_cause: Doctor report publication bypasses the Manager's existing transient Windows sharing-lock classifier/retry/fallback and atomic-publication resilience used by other diagnostic/state writers. A short external lock therefore changes the semantic Doctor outcome instead of being retried or reported distinctly.

evidence.id: Manager 4.17.11 g1 D3 Doctor report sharing violation after all health findings were OK
